title: Spot the Differences
description: Necrosis disguises plant cells as animal cells to confuse you. Learn to tell them apart to seize piece 7's core.

content.value: Plant and animal cells share the basics — both have a cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus and mitochondria. But three clear differences let you tell them apart at a glance.

FEATURE            PLANT CELL     ANIMAL CELL
Cell wall          ✅ yes          ❌ no
Chloroplasts       ✅ yes          ❌ no
Vacuole            ✅ one large    ✅ small (many)
Shape              boxy, regular   round, irregular
Cell membrane      ✅ yes          ✅ yes
Nucleus            ✅ yes          ✅ yes

If a cell has a cell WALL and green CHLOROPLASTS, it's a PLANT cell — and it usually looks neat and box-shaped. If a cell has no cell wall, no chloroplasts, and looks round or irregular, it's an ANIMAL cell.

Because of their rigid cell wall, plant cells have a regular, rectangular shape. Animal cells, held only by a flexible membrane, tend to be round or irregular in shape. Shape alone is often a quick clue.
Quick test: 'Wall + green + big vacuole = PLANT'. 'No wall + round + small vacuoles = ANIMAL'. Both still have membrane, cytoplasm and nucleus.

Key Takeaway: Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and one large vacuole, and are boxy; animal cells lack a wall and chloroplasts, have small vacuoles, and are round. Both share a membrane, cytoplasm and nucleus.

quiz.question: Which is found in a plant cell but NOT an animal cell?
quiz.explain: Chloroplasts (and a cell wall) are found only in plant cells, not animal cells.

quiz.question: Animal cells are usually…
quiz.explain: Without a rigid cell wall, animal cells tend to be round or irregular. Plant cells are boxy.

quiz.question: Which parts do BOTH plant and animal cells have?
quiz.explain: Both cell types share a membrane, cytoplasm and nucleus; only plants add a wall and chloroplasts.
